message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: lint-md

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
  pull_request:

jobs:
  lint-markdown:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set node version
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7

      - name: Install lint-md
        run: npm install -g @lint-md/cli

      - name: Lint markdown
        run: lint-md --suppress-warnings *.md .github/ docs/",
  "rationale": "The workflow has a single job with no explicit timeout. The P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT pattern (bound jobs with a custom timeout) is supported by measured CI workflow evidence showing elapsed savings when adding timeout-minutes: 5 (26.829% in experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508 and 9.790% in experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8). Repository CI history shows successful runs complete in about 12 seconds, so a 5-minute bound provides ample headroom for valid runs while preventing runaway consumption. All triggers, steps, and coverage are preserved; no permissions, secrets, or network access are changed.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508", "experiment:batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8"]
}

      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set node version
        uses: actions/setup-node@v7

      - name: Install lint-md
        run: npm install -g @lint-md/cli

1. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT - Bound jobs with a custom timeout. Evidence shows measured CI workflow on fork with elapsed savings. The experiment examples show adding `timeout-minutes: 5` to jobs. This seems applicable - the workflow has no timeout set, so adding a reasonable timeout could prevent runaway consumption.

- batch-interactive-three--fb8b16eb65a11508: 26.8% elapsed savings, added timeout-minutes: 5
- batch-interactive-three--112e2b2e7fbe04b8: 9.79% elapsed savings, added timeout-minutes: 5

The pattern preconditions: "Representative successful-duration history exists". The CI history shows 5 successful runs, all completing in about 12 seconds. So a timeout of 5 minutes would be very generous headroom.

The contraindications: "Valid slow runs exceed the proposed limit". With runs taking ~12 seconds, a 5-minute timeout is very safe.
